tasks.spec:
You are fixing a batch SMS sender that has never successfully sent a message. BOUNDARY: write only inside your own task directory. Never modify anything outside it. Never call an external API. Never send a message. Never git commit. You own exactly three output files: ./sms_recall_batch.py, ./test_sms_recall_batch.py and ./report.md. Start by copying ./source/sms_recall_batch.py and ./source/test_sms_recall_batch.py into your task directory and editing the copies.

WHAT IS WRONG. The send function posts to /v1/sms/create with a body of phone_number, pathway_id, pathway_version, start_node_id, request_data. Measured against the live Bland API on 2026-07-26: that route rejects even its own documented minimal body with MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELDS, and not one of those field names is accepted. Every campaign this code has ever been pointed at failed silently at this line.

THE CONTRACT THAT WORKS, measured by a successful live send. POST to /v1/sms/send. Required: user_number and agent_number, both E.164. Optional and needed here: request_data for the pathway's variables, new_conversation, pathway_id, pathway_version, start_node_id. There is also an optional agent_message field: OMIT IT. Supplying it sends that literal text instead of letting the pathway compose its own opener, which is the entire point of starting a recall conversation on a pathway.

WHAT TO CHANGE.
(1) Rewrite the send function to use the working route and field names. The recipient becomes user_number.
(2) agent_number is the practice's own SMS line and differs per practice, so it belongs on the ClientProfile dataclass alongside the other per-practice values, not as a literal in the send function. Mott's line is +15095611012. Give CVC's field a value of None and make the sender refuse rather than send if the resolved profile has no number, because sending from the wrong practice's line is worse than not sending.
(3) request_data must keep carrying campaign, store, recall_patient_id and recall_cell. The pathway's first node refuses on an empty store, so losing it dead-ends every conversation.

A THIRD DEFECT YOU MUST NOT PAPER OVER. Two functions read the suppression list by issuing GET requests to the gateway's /sms-suppression route. That route serves POST only; the gateway's GET handler answers exactly two paths and returns 404 for everything else. So the suppression read CANNOT work today and there is no code change that makes it work. Do NOT invent an endpoint, do NOT silently skip the check, and do NOT make the failure non-fatal. Leave the fail-closed refusal exactly as it is, and instead make the situation legible: the refusal message must say plainly that the gateway serves no suppression read, so an operator seeing it knows this is a missing endpoint rather than an outage to retry. Explain this in your report and say what would have to exist to close it.

TESTS. Extend the suite with tests that would have caught this: assert the posted URL, assert the exact payload key set, assert agent_message is absent, assert Mott's agent_number arrives and is not hardcoded in the send function, and assert a profile with no agent_number refuses instead of sending. The existing tests use a fake transport that ignores the auth argument entirely, which is precisely why four separate authentication and contract defects survived a green suite; where a test's fake transport hides a real contract, tighten it.

OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./report.md. Start with '# Sender Contract Fix'. Include '## Summary' with at most 3 bullets, '## What Changed' as a table of function, defect, fix, '## Suppression, Left Broken On Purpose' explaining the missing endpoint and what would close it, '## Tests Added' naming each and what it would have caught, and '## Assumptions'. Under 800 words.

tasks.spec:
You are fixing four failures from a live run of an SMS booking agent, and retiring two tests that assert against fields the system deliberately removed. BOUNDARY: write only inside your own task directory. Never modify anything outside it. Never call an API, never send a message, never mint or deploy a pathway, never git commit. You own exactly four output files: ./build_v57.py, ./v57_graph.json, ./scenarios.py and ./report.md. Copy ./source/build_v56.py and ./source/scenarios.py into your task directory and edit the copies; run your build_v57.py to produce v57_graph.json.

THE EVIDENCE. ./source/LIVE-RUN-OUTPUT.txt is the real output of the 30-scenario suite against the live pathway: 24 passed, 6 failed. Read the failing blocks completely; each names what was expected and what happened.

TWO FAILURES ARE THE TEST'S FAULT, NOT THE CODE'S. The scenarios named 'week plus time of day' and 'clock time with no day at all' assert on captured fields for a part of day and a time floor. Those fields were deliberately deleted from this design because the scheduler was measured to accept and then ignore the parameters they fed, so capturing them only invited values into the wrong slots. Retire those assertions. Do NOT reintroduce the fields to make the tests pass, and do NOT delete the scenarios; keep each scenario exercising whatever it can still legitimately assert, such as where the conversation lands.

FOUR FAILURES ARE REAL. Fix them in the graph.
(a) MOST SERIOUS. When one reply both selects an offered opening and asks for a different time, the agent books the selected one. It must instead ask which the patient meant. Booking a time the patient did not settle on writes a real appointment into a practice schedule, and an earlier defect of exactly this shape is why this system is being audited at all.
(b) A request for a time no slot can satisfy, such as three in the morning, is answered with late-afternoon openings as though they served it. It must say plainly that nothing exists then and ask for another day. Note this is the same substitution failure already fixed once for thin days; the fix there was a distinct offer node whose message names the miss first, and the same shape may apply.
(c) Texting shorthand for a weekday and week, such as a clipped form of 'Tuesday next week', reaches the scheduler verbatim, is rejected, and dead-ends. Extraction must expand common shorthand into the accepted forms. The scheduler accepts a weekday alone, a weekday with a next-week qualifier, a month and a day, or an explicit date, and nothing else.
(d) The fourth failure follows from (b); confirm whether your fix for (b) resolves it and say so either way.

CONSTRAINTS THAT WILL FAIL YOUR WORK IF BROKEN. Only the confirmation node may state that an appointment exists. Every offer node sees exactly two openings and may name no other time. The conflict check must remain structurally impossible to skip before a write. The two opt-out exits must remain reachable only through their suppression call. Prefer a routing or node change over a longer prompt: several rounds of prompt-tightening are already documented as insufficient in this project.

OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./report.md. Start with '# Scenario Fixes'. Include '## Summary' with at most 3 bullets, '## Fixed' as a table of failure, root cause, change made, '## Retired' explaining why the two assertions were wrong rather than the code, '## Nodes Added' if any, and '## Assumptions'. Under 800 words.

Be aware the grading check is a floor, not the gate. It confirms the safety invariants survived and that each fix left real evidence in the artifact. Only a live run of the 30 scenarios can prove the behaviour, and that will be run against your graph afterwards.
